templates.name: Social Queue
templates.title: One idea into a week of unsent posts
templates.tagline: Seven drafts from one idea. Nothing hits the network.
templates.why: Queue tools that auto-post will ship a half-true hook. This Bot fills the week and waits for a human to publish.

templates.name: Thread Scout
templates.title: High-engagement thread craft, original drafts
templates.tagline: Steal the structure. Never steal the post. Never post.
templates.why: "Write a thread like that" usually means plagiarism. This Bot extracts the machine and writes a new one, still unsent.

templates.name: Bug Reproduction
templates.title: Staging reproduction pack writer
templates.tagline: Staging repro packs with evidence — never production customer data.
templates.why: Official Grok Bot use case. Comments guess; this Bot is paid to perform the steps in staging and to stop when it cannot reproduce.

templates.name: Changelog
templates.title: Unreleased notes from merged PRs
templates.tagline: Draft notes from merged PRs — never tag, never publish.
templates.why: Friday archaeology invents "various improvements". This Bot maps every line to a merged PR and leaves publishing to a human.

templates.name: CI Sweeper
templates.title: Report-only CI and flake watcher
templates.tagline: Report failures and flakes — never merge, never hide with reruns.
templates.why: Rerun loops launder flakes into green. This Bot exists so a human sees the flake, the new failure, and the hold — not a manufactured pass.

templates.name: Docs Drift
templates.title: README and API docs vs code
templates.tagline: Draft the doc diff — never commit, never rewrite code to match.
templates.why: Stale READMEs ship the wrong contract to every new hire. This Bot cites both paths and leaves the merge to a human.

templates.name: Issue Drafter
templates.title: Unsent GitHub issue writer
templates.tagline: Slack and repro packs become unsent issues — never auto-filed.
templates.why: Threads rot. This Bot exists so title, expected, actual, and steps are in the tracker shape before anyone clicks Submit.

templates.name: PR Reviewer
templates.title: Risk-first pull request reviewer
templates.tagline: Review starts at the scary diff, not the title.
templates.why: Title-first review rubber-stamps. This Bot leads with breakage, missing tests, and description-vs-diff gaps.

templates.name: Query Helper
templates.title: Schema-grounded SQL drafter
templates.tagline: Draft SQL from the schema — never run writes on a live database.
templates.why: Chat-invented columns wreck production. This Bot quotes the schema it read and leaves execution of writes to a human.

templates.name: Repo Hardener
templates.title: Security and hygiene recommender
templates.tagline: Recommend issues and PRs — never push main, never edit protection.
templates.why: Drive-by "hardening" that flips protection settings is an outage. This Bot reports what is off and leaves the click to a human.

templates.name: SaaS Finance
templates.title: Weekly collected-revenue memo
templates.tagline: Collected, renewing, past-due — a memo, not a collections bot.
templates.why: Weekly SaaS numbers hide in billing mail. This Bot totals what the mail actually shows, compares to last week's memo, and will not dunn a customer or issue a credit to "make the week look right".

templates.name: Security Questionnaire
templates.title: Draft answers from the pack
templates.tagline: Cited drafts from the pack — the Submit button stays human.
templates.why: Questionnaires get answered from memory and then contradict last quarter's pack. This Bot drafts from the pack, lists what the pack does not say, and will not submit.

templates.name: AEO Watch
templates.title: Answer-engine visibility as a standing program
templates.tagline: A query set on a cadence — not "hey ChatGPT, do we show up".
templates.why: One screenshot of an overview is an anecdote. This Bot reruns the same queries, diffs citations, and writes a brief a search lead can review.

templates.name: Brand Watch
templates.title: Mention digest from Slack and X
templates.tagline: A reading pile, not a reply thread.
templates.why: Brand bots that "jump in" create support tickets. This one collates what was said and leaves the reply to a person.

templates.name: Competitor Watch
templates.title: Material-change competitor watch
templates.tagline: Alert only when the page actually changed. Silence is a result.
templates.why: Daily competitor recaps train people to ignore them. This Bot diffs against last snapshot and speaks only when the number or the sentence moved.

templates.name: Content Remix
templates.title: Draft-only social and email variants
templates.tagline: One draft in. A set of variants out. Nothing ships.
templates.why: Remixing in the composer produces five slightly different tweets and a live accident. This Bot returns a pack the owner can reject by heading.

templates.name: Newsletter Desk
templates.title: Unsent weekly newsletter from saved links
templates.tagline: The issue is written. The send button stays with the owner.
templates.why: Newsletter tools want a cadence more than a spine. This Bot collates what was already saved and stops at a reviewable issue.

templates.name: Paid Media
templates.title: Spend, CAC, and reallocation drafts
templates.tagline: Numbers and a Slack draft. The budget does not move itself.
templates.why: Official Grok Bot use case: analysis first, campaign changes behind approval even after the memo becomes a routine.

templates.name: Foundry
templates.title: Grok Bot template foundry
templates.tagline: One job in, a shippable Bot recipe out — not a cute persona.
templates.why: Most shared Bots fail as General Helper with no boundary. Foundry exists so the next Bot you create is already L1, sourced, and share-safe.

templates.name: Memory Gardener
templates.title: Stale-memory corrector
templates.tagline: Correct stale memory against a source — do not wipe the role.
templates.why: Bots treat chat memory as policy. This one exists so changing facts live in a source system, and the description only holds rules that stay true.

templates.name: Setup
templates.title: Catalog installer
templates.tagline: Paste START.md, tap a team, get a roster — not a catalog dump.
templates.why: People stall on the first Bot. Setup exists so a team appears with descriptions that already encode L1 boundaries.

templates.name: Roster Coach
templates.title: Smallest-useful fleet auditor
templates.tagline: Cut and merge first — never grow the fleet past the ask.
templates.why: Accounts stall at the combined Bot and group cap. This Bot exists so the next move is a cut, not another catch-all teammate.

templates.name: Fleet Router
templates.title: One-owner work dispatcher
templates.tagline: Pick one owner, hand off, go silent — never do the work.
templates.why: Group chats stall when every Bot answers. This Bot exists so work has one throat to choke and the human sees a single review point.

templates.name: Share Sanitizer
templates.title: Public-share secret stripper
templates.tagline: Redact first — the share link must not carry secrets or customers.
templates.why: A public share copies identity, description, skills, and routines. It does not copy the computer, but pasted keys and Acme customer names still leak.

templates.name: Chief of Staff
templates.title: Source-linked daily digest
templates.tagline: Only items that map to the priority list — with a decision flag.
templates.why: Official use case. Untuned CoS bots dump every channel. This one is useful only after the owner marks noise, then it earns a weekday routine.

templates.name: Cloud Spend
templates.title: Cloud bill notes, not console edits
templates.tagline: Movers and recommendations — the console stays closed.
templates.why: Bill shock shows up in mail first. This Bot writes the note with the invoice as denominator and will not open the cloud console to "fix" it.

templates.name: Expense Manager
templates.title: Weekly expense recon with policy cites
templates.tagline: Totals that reconcile — exceptions that cite the signed policy.
templates.why: Official use case. Untuned expense bots invent categories and send chases. This one reconciles to the source, cites the signed policy, and stops at drafts until a human is happy with the week.

templates.name: Incident Desk
templates.title: Slack-and-GitHub incident timeline
templates.tagline: A timeline a skeptic can audit — not a production console.
templates.why: Incident channels go stale in an hour. This Bot turns Slack and GitHub into a chronological write-up a human can accept or reject, and it will not touch prod while it does it.

templates.name: New Hire Ramp
templates.title: First-week plan with unsent holds
templates.tagline: A week-one plan a manager can edit — invites stay in draft.
templates.why: Ramp docs die as a wall of links. This Bot produces a day-by-day plan with owners and unsent holds so the manager still does the inviting.

templates.name: Vendor Inbox
templates.title: Invoice and renewal work list
templates.tagline: A vendor work list, not a chase bot.
templates.why: AP inboxes hide renewals under newsletters. This Bot extracts a list a human can pay from, drafts the missing-info notes, and does not send them.

templates.name: Calendar Defender
templates.title: Deep-work block protector
templates.tagline: Draft the decline. Never move the meeting yourself.
templates.why: A helper that "just declines" will drop a customer QBR. This Bot shows the collision and waits.

templates.name: Inbox Triage
templates.title: Inbox zero without living in Gmail
templates.tagline: Buckets and drafts — never send, never delete, never unsubscribe.
templates.why: Inbox-zero tools that send are a liability. This Bot sorts and drafts so the human still owns every outbound message.

templates.name: Subscription Audit
templates.title: Unused-subscription watch from mail
templates.tagline: Evidence of last use, then a list — you click cancel.
templates.why: Auto-unsubscribe bots cancel the wrong vendor. This Bot builds the list and waits for approval, especially in week one.

templates.name: Travel Desk
templates.title: Itinerary sanity without booking
templates.tagline: Sanity-check the trip. Never book. Never pay.
templates.why: A travel helper with a card on file is an incident. This Bot compares options and stops at the review pack.

templates.name: Evidence Packager
templates.title: Ship-or-block evidence compiler
templates.tagline: Package what was verified — never issue the ship or block.
templates.why: Runs end with a story. This Bot exists so claims without artifact pointers stay unverified, and the human still owns ship or block.

templates.name: Feature Ask Collator
templates.title: Clustered product asks, not a roadmap
templates.tagline: Quotes and counts. You do not ship the roadmap.
templates.why: Slack "we should" threads multiply. This Bot clusters the job-to-be-done and stops before anyone files or prioritizes.

templates.name: Launch Coordinator
templates.title: Go/no-go packet, never the publish
templates.tagline: One owner per role. The human issues the ship verdict.
templates.why: Launch chats spawn duplicate posts. This Bot assigns, tracks, and refuses to hit publish.

templates.name: Product Performance
templates.title: Evidence-backed performance investigations
templates.tagline: Hotspot, links, facts vs hypotheses — never touch production.
templates.why: Official use case. Latency chats guess. This Bot opens the charts, names the hotspot, and stops before anyone pages or flips a flag.

templates.name: Cited Brief
templates.title: Three-minute cited brief
templates.tagline: One question, three minutes, every claim has a URL.
templates.why: Research Desk goes deep. This Bot is the short brief you can read before a meeting without inventing numbers.

templates.name: Research Desk
templates.title: Cited research with a not-found list
templates.tagline: Claims, evidence, disagreements, not-found — then a next read.
templates.why: Answer engines average. This Bot is paid to show the fight between sources and to admit gaps.

templates.name: Source Interrogator
templates.title: Assumption hunter for briefs and memos
templates.tagline: Find the load-bearing claim that never had a source.
templates.why: Teams ship on sentences that sound like facts. This Bot is paid to break those sentences before they become a plan.

templates.name: Call Follow-up
templates.title: Unsent recap and tasks after a call
templates.tagline: Recap and tasks, still in the building. Sending is a later named L2.
templates.why: Official Grok Bot shape: read-and-prepare first. Follow-up mail sent in the moment forgets who promised what. This Bot writes the pack and waits.

templates.name: Meeting Prep
templates.title: Pre-call brief from CRM, mail, and calendar
templates.tagline: Walk in knowing the last promise — the customer already lived the rest.
templates.why: Forgotten commitments reopen closed arguments. This Bot rebuilds the thread privately and stops before anyone outside the company sees it.

templates.name: Outbound
templates.title: Account research and review-ready outreach
templates.tagline: Volume without sounding like a sequence tool — and without sending.
templates.why: Official Grok Bot use case: research and drafts first, nightly routine only after the review list is reliable. Sending is a later, named L2.

templates.name: Talent Scout
templates.title: Candidate sourcing and unsent outreach
templates.tagline: Twenty names with evidence. Outreach stays in the draft folder.
templates.why: Official Grok Bot use case: research and drafts first. Contacting anyone is a later, named L2 after privacy and source terms are checked.

templates.name: Win Loss
templates.title: Win/loss memos from notes and CRM
templates.tagline: Pattern with evidence. Not "they just weren't ready".
templates.why: Closed-lost reasons rot into adjectives. This Bot writes a memo other reps can act on and leaves the lost account alone.

templates.name: Account Health
templates.title: Ranked portfolio watch list
templates.tagline: Evidence-ranked watch list — no customer mail, no CRM edits.
templates.why: Official use case. Untuned health bots email customers and write vibes into the CRM. This one ranks against saved thresholds and stops at a list a human can act on.

templates.name: Promise Log
templates.title: Customer commitments, written down
templates.tagline: Quotes and dates — not a customer recap email.
templates.why: Commitments vanish between the call and the next QBR. This Bot appends them to a workspace log with a quote, and it will not mail the customer a recap that creates still more promises.

templates.name: Support Replies
templates.title: Policy-cited first-response drafts
templates.tagline: A DRAFT reply with a policy cite — the Send button stays yours.
templates.why: First responses rot in the queue while people hunt the help center. This Bot drafts against the policy source of truth and will not send, refund, or "make them whole" on its own.

teams.name: Eng
teams.why: Staging reports stall when repro, the unsent issue, and the risk review live in one undifferentiated chat.

teams.name: Loop
teams.why: Inner-loop coding agents still need an outer evidence/verdict loop before anyone merges, tags, or writes the ship rationale.

teams.name: Marketing
teams.why: Competitor noise, channel variants, and the weekly issue get mixed until someone diffs, remixes, and still does not publish.

teams.name: Meta
teams.why: Standing up a catalog team, cutting a bloated fleet, routing work, and minting the next contract are four jobs, not one Setup dump.

teams.name: Ops
teams.why: The week hides in Slack, receipts, and vendor mail until someone maps it to priorities without sending a chase.

teams.name: Personal
teams.why: Inbox zero fails when mail, meetings, and unused subs are one Bot that is tempted to send, decline, and unsubscribe.

teams.name: Product
teams.why: Latency, Slack asks, and launch day collide unless one Bot owns evidence, one clusters asks, and one refuses to publish.

teams.name: Research
teams.why: Deep briefs, three-minute answers, and assumption hunts are different jobs; mixing them hides the not-found list.

teams.name: Sales
teams.why: Outbound volume is useless if the next call is unbriefed and the recap never gets written down before it is sent.

teams.name: Success
teams.why: Renewals slip when health is a vibe, replies go out uncited, and promises evaporate after the call.

patterns.name: Description vs message
patterns.summary: Standing rules live in the Bot description. This-task instructions live in the conversation. Descriptions survive new threads; messages do not.

patterns.name: Draft then routine
patterns.summary: Start with a one-time task. Make it reliable. Save a skill. Test a second input. Create a routine only when retries and failure cases are defined.

patterns.name: Duplicate for scope, not security
patterns.summary: Duplicate a Bot when you want the same role for a different scope — one Account Health per region. The copy gets profile, skills, routines, avatar — not history or memory.

patterns.name: Evidence-bearing results
patterns.summary: For consequential work, separate facts, inferences, completed actions, actions waiting for approval, and unresolved questions. Preserve links.

patterns.name: Group for visible handoffs
patterns.summary: Use a group when several Bots need one shared outcome and visible handoffs. Two to six Bots. One owner per stage. @mentions.

patterns.name: No-data / stale-data policy
patterns.summary: If the source is unavailable, report the failure instead of using old data. Missing CI is "CI not found", not "tests look fine".

patterns.name: One job per Bot
patterns.summary: Create a separate Bot when the work has a distinct goal, tools, working style, approval boundary, or schedule. Catch-all helpers produce weak memory.

patterns.name: Sanitize before you share
patterns.summary: A public share link copies identity, description, skills, and routines. It does not copy your computer. Still: strip secrets first.

patterns.name: Shared computer is not isolation
patterns.summary: Every Bot on an account uses the same cloud computer — cookies, files, CLI credentials. Separate Bots are not a security boundary.

patterns.name: Skill six fields
patterns.summary: A useful skill states when to use it, inputs, sequence, how to validate, what to return, and what requires approval.

patterns.name: Smallest useful roster
patterns.summary: Give one Bot ownership of an end-to-end outcome. Add another only when the work has a stable specialist role. Cap installer teams at four.

patterns.name: Standing approval boundary
patterns.summary: Tell the Bot which actions it can take and where it must stop. Prefer explicit boundaries for send, publish, pay, delete, permissions, production, and legal terms.
